sentences.text: East Service Lift runs a door-interlock and overload check before accepting a movement request.
The Field Supervisor coordinates the inspection before the first planned movement of each operating shift.
The inspection begins with a visual check of the car, landing doors, guide surfaces, and access barriers.
The inspector confirms that the car floor and landing thresholds are clear of loose material and standing water.
Door interlocks are tested at each served landing to confirm that the car cannot move while a door is open.
The emergency stop and alarm are tested using the approved functional test procedure.
The inspector checks the operating controls for damage, legibility, and secure mounting.
The hoist, suspension points, and visible cable sections are examined for wear, corrosion, or abnormal movement.
The Electrical Technician verifies that the lift supply and protective devices show no active fault indication.
The inspector confirms that the rated capacity and operating instructions remain legible at the car entrance.
The Field Supervisor records the inspection result and any observed defects in the maintenance system.
A defect affecting safe operation prevents release until the required repair and verification are complete.
The Work Permit Portal is checked for active restrictions that could conflict with lift operation.
The Duty Planner confirms that the planned work can proceed within the lift capacity and operating limits.
Personnel are briefed on the permitted landings, maximum occupancy, and emergency actions before boarding.
The Personnel Tracking Console is used to maintain an accurate record of personnel entering and leaving the route.
Equipment is inspected for dimensions, mass, and secure packaging before it is accepted for transport.
The Storekeeper confirms that equipment intended for the lift is ready and properly identified for the work party.
Long or unstable loads are not carried unless an approved handling arrangement keeps the load contained within the car.
The operator positions each load to avoid obstructing doors, controls, and emergency access.
The Field Supervisor confirms that no person is exposed to a suspended or shifting load during movement.
The release decision is based on a satisfactory inspection, valid work authorization, and compliance with stated limits.
The Field Supervisor communicates the release status to the work party and records the time that service is authorized.
During operation, users report unusual noise, vibration, door behavior, or control response immediately.
The lift is removed from service if a new condition could compromise safe movement, pending assessment and corrective action.
